chapters.title: What Is a Crucial Conversation and Why Should I Care?
chapters.sourcePressure: Crucial conversations are moments of high stakes, opposing views, and strong emotion where avoidance or clumsy handling creates the downstream damage people later call bad luck.
chapters.coreMove: Recognize a consequential conversation before you dodge it or dump emotion into it.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the opening as a generic celebration of brave honesty or conflict confidence.

chapters.title: Mastering Crucial Conversations: The Power of Dialogue
chapters.sourcePressure: Dialogue works by enlarging the Pool of Shared Meaning; silence shrinks the pool, decisions weaken, and later resistance often comes from meaning that never entered the room.
chapters.coreMove: Diagnose whether the shared pool is filling or whether missing meaning is already shaping the outcome.
chapters.commonMisread: Making dialogue sound like polite turn-taking instead of a decision-quality mechanism.

chapters.title: Start with Heart: Focus on What You Really Want
chapters.sourcePressure: Before speaking, the reader must notice how pressure quietly changes their goal from solving the problem to saving face, punishing, escaping, or proving a point.
chapters.coreMove: Reset your aim mid-heat by asking what you really want for yourself, the other person, and the relationship.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing the skill to staying calm or being nice.

chapters.title: Master My Stories: Staying in Dialogue When You're Upset
chapters.sourcePressure: The Path to Action inserts a story between facts and feelings, exposing victim, villain, and helpless stories as editable interpretations rather than direct reality.
chapters.coreMove: Work backward from your reaction to the story you told, then separate facts from interpretation before acting.
chapters.commonMisread: Teaching readers to distrust emotion or suppress anger.

chapters.title: Learn to Look: Watch for When the Conversation Turns Crucial
chapters.sourcePressure: The reader must watch content and conditions at once, catching safety loss through silence or violence before the conversation is already flooded.
chapters.coreMove: Shift attention from the topic to the conditions and name the exact silence or violence move as it starts.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the chapter into a checklist of body-language clues.

chapters.title: Make It Safe: How to Make It Safe to Talk About Almost Anything
chapters.sourcePressure: Safety is restored by diagnosing whether Mutual Purpose or Mutual Respect is missing, then using apology, contrasting, or CRIB sincerely and in the right order.
chapters.coreMove: Repair the safety break before continuing the hard message.
chapters.commonMisread: Making safety repair sound like softening the truth until nobody objects.

chapters.title: STATE My Path: How to Speak Persuasively, Not Abrasively
chapters.sourcePressure: STATE structures a hard message: facts first, owned story second, invitation third, tentative language throughout, and active encouragement for testing.
chapters.coreMove: Put a difficult story into the pool without presenting it as a verdict.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating STATE as a polished feedback sandwich or a way to sound less harsh while accusing someone.

chapters.title: Explore Others' Paths: How to Listen When Others Blow Up or Clam Up
chapters.sourcePressure: When the other person is silent or explosive, AMPP draws their path out, then ABC keeps disagreement narrow by agreeing, building, or comparing.
chapters.coreMove: Invite the other person back into dialogue by making their path speakable before you respond to it.
chapters.commonMisread: Making listening sound like passive empathy or letting the other person dominate.

chapters.title: Move to Action: Turning Crucial Conversations Into Results
chapters.sourcePressure: Conversation only becomes results when the group chooses an explicit decision method and closes with Who does What by When and Follow-up.
chapters.coreMove: Turn apparent agreement into accountable action by naming the decision mode and the follow-up owner.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the close as productivity task management detached from dialogue.

chapters.title: Yeah, But: Tough Cases and Putting It All Together
chapters.sourcePressure: Tough cases change the order and emphasis of the same framework; the framework fails when used to win, manipulate, or sound reasonable while refusing to be changed.
chapters.coreMove: Adapt the sequence to the difficult case while staying genuinely open to being changed by what enters the pool.
chapters.commonMisread: Offering special tricks for difficult personalities or power plays.
